metadata.title: A Galaxy Law Tied to Dark Energy, and a Map of What It Leaves Unexplained (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.1 (2026-11-02). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; not reproduced by any outside group. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed; nothing here says the data favour this framework over any other.

A programme report after its own final grade. The galaxy law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), with a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_DE), is MOND's simple form with a proposed origin for its scale, proposed earlier by other authors. It describes isolated disc galaxies well on the canonical footing, and its tie to dark energy has no decisive test yet. It fails IC 1613, several Local Group classes, cluster shear, X-COP (factor 2.93) and the unscreened Solar System, its Milky Way result depends on a vertical form it doesn't supply, and it has no action and no account of the CMB. The cold sector built to cover those failed on measured data and is retired. The note gives the scorecard, the two walls, the covariant attempts on record, twelve requirements for any successor and the dated tests that can still kill the law. It is numerical evidence for the families tried, not a no-go theorem.

Version 1.1 adds lanes run after the retirement; none was blind, all were run by AI subagents, and no outside group has reproduced them. AR1 landed, MOVES AND FAILS, conditional on one missed check. A gas term fitted on X-COP reaches 14 of 15 keys on the canonical footing (fragile, never 15; alt 10), and tied to present gas it is dead on the Bullet. Published AeST, action searches, a one-component requirement calculation and a 96-row harness are reported; all fail or are empty for what was listed, and none of this is a no-go theorem. A repaired test gives no statistical support that the a0 formula is special (5.51 bits, FDR-DEAD; 92.7 % of scrambled scalars decompose as simply); that doesn't refute it, and the test lacks power at 16.6 % precision. Correction to v1.0: v9's alpha_1 = -2(K_B+2) is a static-branch ratio; a moving source has alpha_1 = alpha_2 = 0 at G = G~, and v9 stays non-viable because it loses the law for moving systems. Added: MUSE-DARK III reports a0 rising with redshift, which counts against the flat band at face value. Alcock (MNRAS 2026) puts Lambda-tied frameworks under the same pressure. We read the rise as mass-route dependent and not decisive; on the survey's masses the band fails.
